subject: Proposal: reserved H100 pool + capacity increase for Q3 renewal
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@bluelake.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Proposal: reserved H100 pool + capacity increase for Q3 renewal
Attachments: BL-4582-draft-proposal.pdf (proposal, 3 pages)

Hi Elaine —

Thanks again for the deep dive last week. Based on your forecasted Q3 usage (stable 80% utilization, peak bursts to 95%), I've sketched a renewal that combines a 12-month reserved pool and an incremental 20 H100 GPUs to replace the current A100 reservation. The attached draft lays out pricing, throughput guarantees, and the proposed amendment language for the renewal.

Key highlights (TL;DR):
- Reserved pool: 120 GPUs total (baseline) with +20 H100 dedicated uplift for LLM inference bursts.
- Guarantee: 95th percentile tail latency SLO for your top-10 routes; throughput target scaled to your QPS profile.
- Hardware change: A100 -> H100 (or optional L40S) with per-GPU perf/cost comparison included.

I wanted to surface the perf-per-dollar rationale early: H100 gives ~1.8–2.4x throughput for our attention-heavy models versus A100 at similar quantization profiles; the net cost per generated token usually drops for high-throughput services because you need fewer devices and less batching overhead. I asked product to attach concrete metric tables.

Would you like us to price the L40S alternative side-by-side, or should we proceed with H100 as the recommended baseline? Happy to schedule a 30-min call with engineering ops to walk the numbers.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

--
Redwood Inference — Production-grade inference for engineering teams

Rishi —

Appreciate the fast turnaround and summary. A couple quick clarifying questions before procurement starts the paperwork: 

1) Can you provide performance-per-dollar estimates for both H100 and L40S vs our current A100 baseline (we run the 'dialogue-v0' variant primarily)? Specifically: tokens/sec per GPU, estimated tokens/$ for our QPS profile, and expected change in average latency at our 4096 context.

2) Procurement asked about contract term flexibility: will Redwood allow a 9-month ramp in committed GPUs (we may want to start with +10 and move to +20 after month 3)? Any pricing cliff or step discounts?

3) Are there any migration operational risks (model recompilation, quantization re-tuning) and a rough timeline for cutover?

If you can send a short write-up for points 1–3, procurement can start the amendment review. If easier, let's do a 30-min call Monday.

Best,
Elaine Park

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 14:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposal: reserved H100 pool + capacity increase for Q3 renewal
Attachments: perf-metrics-H100-vs-A100.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Hi team —

Attached is the short perf packet. High-level findings (summary):

- tokens/sec (dialogue-v0, 4096 context, batch=8 local inference profile):
  - A100 (current): ~18.5k tokens/sec per GPU
  - H100: ~37.0k tokens/sec per GPU (x2.0)
  - L40S: ~31.5k tokens/sec per GPU (x1.7)

- tokens per USD (per GPU, normalized to your committed pricing tiers in the draft):
  - A100: baseline 1.0x
  - H100: ~1.75x cost-efficiency (i.e., you get ~75% more tokens for similar spend when accounting for fewer GPUs needed and lower batching overhead)
  - L40S: ~1.55x cost-efficiency vs A100

- 95th percentile latency (single-request, cold KV miss scenario):
  - A100: ~210 ms
  - H100: ~120 ms
  - L40S: ~140 ms

Operational notes for migration:
- Model rebuild: dialogue-v0 requires a quick quantization profile re-check on H100 (we recommend an overnight validation job). Typical runtime: 6–10 hours for your model suite.
- KV cache behavior: identical across HW classes; no changes to prefix caching APIs required.
- Rollout plan (phased):
  1) Provision +10 H100 as warm pool (no traffic) and run canary tests (48 hours).
  2) Route 10–20% traffic through H100 over 1 week, monitor tail latency and quality.
  3) If metrics hold, move to +20 after month 3 and decommission equivalent A100 capacity.

Pricing/tiers: a staged ramp can be accommodated. Pricing cliff: 10–20 GPU step triggers the next discount tier in our reserved pricing matrix; we can lock rates on a 12-month amendment but allow a single scheduled resize within Q1. Exact tier numbers are in the attached spreadsheet and the draft proposal.

Recommendation: H100 for BlueLake's heavy attention workloads — it reduces unit cost and materially improves tail latency. L40S is a lower-cost alternative with good throughput but slightly higher latency.

Happy to jump on the Monday call if you want to walk the numbers.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
